status_explanation: HIGH_PRIORITY_REVIEW: Multi-evidence bi-temporal change detected across 3280 pixels (20.0% of AOI) with sharp vegetation loss (ΔNDVI <= -0.1) and bare soil/rock exposure between 2021-02-05 and 2021-02-10 on hazardous mountain slopes (MODERATE_SLOPE_HAZARD, mean slope 27.0°). Immediate geotechnical review recommended. Raw CNN v2 output: 1.0000 (uncalibrated activation).
assessment_type_explanation: This assessment evaluates surface disturbance between paired satellite observations. It is a post-event disturbance screening tool, NOT a pre-event predictive early warning system, and does NOT forecast the exact timing of future slope failures.

recommended_actions: Dispatch field geotechnical survey to inspect valley runout and slope stability.
Acquire cloud-free high-resolution commercial or aerial imagery.
Query Sentinel-1 SAR C-band radar coherence loss to verify surface displacement.

cnn_inference_diagnostics.scientific_warning: Sigmoid score represents uncalibrated mathematical activation, NOT posterior probability. Single-image CNN v2 has 0% validated specificity on Indian healthy vegetation.

bi_temporal_change_detection.summary_description: Detected sharp vegetation loss (ΔNDVI <= -0.1) and bare soil exposure across 3280 pixels (20.0% of AOI).
caveats: Optical change detection reflects land surface alteration but cannot distinguish landslides from agricultural clearing, intentional logging, or seasonal phenology without terrain context.
Cloud shadows or subtle atmospheric differences between passes can induce minor localized NDVI fluctuations.

terrain_topography_context.interpretation: Mean terrain slope of 27.0° classified as MODERATE_SLOPE_HAZARD. Steep terrain (>15°) supports initiation; flatter valley terrain (<15°) can host debris deposition.

limitations_and_missing_evidence: Optical Sentinel-2 imagery cannot detect terrain beneath dense cloud cover (frequent during monsoon season).
Single-image optical classification cannot differentiate historical bare rock cliffs from fresh landslides without bi-temporal change.
Bi-temporal optical change detection can capture non-landslide surface disturbances (agricultural harvesting, logging, fires).
This microservice is an experimental geospatial prototype and must NOT be used as an autonomous life-safety early warning system.
